## E2: world-aware reading, veto first then choice (2026-11-12)

- **What was built** (option `worldAware: off | veto | choose | observe | veto-strict | choose-strict`, default off; `PSYS2_WORLD_AWARE`, `scripts/e1-collect.mjs --world-aware`). Spec: `specs/16-world-aware-reading.md`. Code: `src/dialog/world-aware.mjs`; `ReasonerSession.score` and `peek` (read-only, the library's `score` and `rank`); a `pick` hook in the rule formalizer (`readGroup`); optional read-only `checkReferents` hooks in `art.draw` and `diagram.sketch`. Tests: `tests/world-aware.test.mjs` (12). Measurement: `scripts/e2-world-aware.mjs`; results `training/results/e2-world-aware-2026-11-12.{json,md}` (every changed case, per set, both modes).
- **Veto reasons** (default `veto`): `no-referent` (the world has no such thing: "delete the dragon" lists what IS in the picture; "connect Start to End" with no End: "There is no shape called End. Shall I add it?" and a "yes" does it), `no-game` (a move in a game that is not running, asked from another tab), `words-best-effort` (a guess of loose words that leaves content words out becomes "Did you mean ...?"). "switch to klingon" answers with the languages from the ui.shell kb. `words-partial` (the partial-understanding window) is only in the `-strict` modes: it loses more right answers than it prevents wrong ones.
- **Numbers** (about 8,430 judged messages; right / wrong / not understood). rules: off 7263 / 431 / 650, veto 7261 / 398 / 685, choose 7267 / 399 / 683, veto-strict 7194 / 361 / 790. encoder+n1 (shipped): off 7436 / 482 / 485, veto 7439 / 456 / 509, choose 7439 / 456 / 510, veto-strict 7386 / 420 / 598. veto against off: wrong to not understood 28 (rules) and 22 (encoder+n1), wrong to right 5 and 6, right to not understood 7 and 3. **Gate met: no new wrong in veto and choose, both modes** (the first runs had 6 and 1: the sibling hold, and a `no-game` veto of the spurious reading of a correction, both fixed). veto-strict has one new wrong (a dialogue turn that rests on a dropped earlier turn).
- **Named cases.** Fixed in veto/choose: "fă părul roșu" (no longer "make it red": now not understood, the reading that dropped "părul" lost), "connect Start to End", "delete the dragon", "switch to klingon", "put it in the top right corner" on the Drawing tab (veto: no game is running; choose: moves the house). Not changed, and why: "give it a hat made of cheese", "center and what is 3 times 3", "colour Spain in" (now "There is no Spain in the picture", safe but the map has Spain), "add milk ... and also can penguins fly", "ce poți face pe hartă?", "înapoi": the right reading is not among the readings the formalizers found, or the world has no hook yet.
- **Library order against the host.** The library's default `rank` counts the answer a question cannot give yet as a lack: it would put a statement that tells nonsense ("a gretel goes what") before the question "what did gretel say". The host zeroes `lacks` for question readings (6 Romanian total questions differ; the router's reading was right in all six); `libraryDefault` is recorded in every pick. A move in an idle game comes last (14 reorderings applied; rules only). In encoder+n1 the library's order and the host's agree everywhere.
- **Honest limits.** (1) `score` returns `judged = false` for most readings: the matrices declare few actions (spec 15), so the library alone seldom separates two readings; `no-referent` and `no-game` read the worlds' hooks and the session context. (2) Choice is over the rules' top readings and the best-effort candidates only. Not done: the dispatcher's top-k (one reading per clause), the library's split candidates (class h: `interpret` needs `core.word` facts, none exist yet: E3 item 2), the dialogue layer's follow-up readings (the discourse layer mutates its state before it reads), the translator route. (3) Romanian is not E2's: the words the translator leaves of three letters or fewer count as function words, the rest as content. (4) The one word-level veto that works is the best-effort one; for the rest no cheap feature separates harmful from harmless dropped words (questions read as commands: 11 right against 6 wrong).
- **For the user (no default changed).** `veto` looks safe to turn on: it never added a wrong answer and turned 28 wrong answers into not understood (22) or right (6) in the shipped mode, for 3 right answers lost. `choose` adds a little on top. The world hooks are the part that scales: each world that writes `checkReferents` gets state-aware refusals; today two do.
## NAMESPACES: fact namespaces on sopworld 0.9.0 (2026-11-12)

- **Done.** (1) Every library instance is a World with its own namespace (`session.conversation`, each game, each tab); `src/reasoner/ns.mjs` hands it out with bare ids in and out (qualify what goes in, strip what comes out, `{ ns }` on queries) and gives the action functions of `fns.mjs` the same through `nsContext`; the timeline record is `v: 2` (the library log holds qualified ids; a v1 record is refused as unreadable). (2) Ids made in a turn carry it: `FormSession.turn`, `t12_w3` (the counter is still the session's). Tests: `tests/reasoner-namespaces.test.mjs` (two "I buy a ball" turns are two purchases with the turn in their ids; two draw objects of one name are two; the diagram refuses the second shape of a name; the library keeps two namespaces apart and merges inside one). (3) `shared=true` is declared for `core.agent` (what every instance reads); `reads=` is used by no world, so there is no `exports=` to write (the library's `exports=` is for `core.module`, which the worlds are not). (4) `world.warnings` of every instance, reported once per session: `reply.warnings`, debug view "Library warnings", phrase log `detail.warnings`. (5) Spec 15, "Namespaces".
- **Gates.** `npm test` 1,437 pass, 0 fail (loop guard included); `test-world all` clean in both reasoners; `build-webchat.mjs` run; Chrome `test-webchat-matrix` and `test:browser` below.
- **dump-turns before/after, 4,591 turns.** 4,262 turns identical; 277 differ only by the turn prefix in ids inside the state (`t1_w1` for `w1`); the 52 others are the known random turns (media.music picks a song, ui.avatar a seed: 5 + 1 + 46 turns) and 46 `ui.avatar` states whose pending request has a `span.end` 3 longer (the id grew by `t1_`). Intended differences: the ids, nothing else. Replies, statuses and every other state: identical.
- **Bench** (`bench-reasoner.mjs --reps 3`, 12,072 turns; the old tree from `git archive HEAD` and the new tree at the same time on the same loaded machine; p50 ms, ops / matrix, matrix minus ops): all 9.1 / 11.0, +1.9 before and 9.2 / 11.8, +2.7 after (second run on 700 cases per set: +2.1 -> +2.5). Groups, full run: four +2.1 -> +3.5, kids-other +1.6 -> +2.7, music/draw/map/charts +2.0 -> +2.7, games +2.7 -> +3.8, documents +1.8 -> +2.6, avatar/shell/editor +1.6 -> +1.7. The cost is the library's (`_nsUsed` adds the namespace to every match) plus the facade's walk over results; the facade is capped in depth and allocates only where an id is found.
- **Library items (sopworld 0.9.0), each with a minimal repro** (scripts in the session scratchpad; the numbers are what 0.9.0 does):
  1. `replace(id, text)` in a world with `ns` puts the new wire in the default namespace when the id in `text` is a bare one: `w = new World({ ns: 'A' }); w.load('@t core.type\n@t.k core.slot of=t key=k kind=number'); w.tell('@x t k=1'); w.replace('A::x', '@x t k=2'); [...w.wires.keys()]` gives `['x']`, expected `['A::x']`. (The host writes the qualified id.)
  2. The result of a `core.aggregate` is told in the default namespace, not in that of the counted wires, so a rule or deny that joins it with the namespace's facts never matches: `w = new World({ ns: 'A' })`, load `@block core.type`, a `core.aggregate over=$bk by=?k count=?c then=$hk` into `have kind=?k count=?c`, a deny `when=$w2 not=$wh2` (want / have by kind), tell `@b1 block kind=paragraph`: the `have` wire is `_hk_...` (default namespace) and `check` of a `want kind=paragraph` is refused ("There is no paragraph"). It passes when `have` is `shared=true`. (docs.editor therefore stays in the default namespace: `NO_NAMESPACE` in `ns.mjs`.)
  3. A type declared through `core.schema.map` (every type of our legends) ignores `shared=`, `transient=` and `unique=`: only a native `core.type` reads them (`!f &&` in the compile of types). `m.load('@map core.schema.map from=mytype as=type name=id shared=shared'); m.load('@agent mytype shared=true'); m._compiled().shared` is empty; with `@agent core.type shared=true` it holds `agent`. The map needs `shared=`, `transient=`, `unique=` fields.
  4. A log entry does not keep the namespace it was told in, so a replay qualifies it again: `w.tell('@e.user agent', { ns: '' })` on a world with `ns: 'A'`, then `_replay(w.log)` on a second world with `ns: 'A'` gives `A::e.user` (the original holds `e.user`). `World.restore`/`_replay` should store `ns` per entry. (The host rewrites the entry to `::e.user` while it replays: `replayInto`.)
  5. A reference without a namespace to a fact of a `shared=true` type that exists only in the default namespace does not resolve ("references local first" stops at the namespace): `@agent core.type shared=true`, `w.tell('@e.user agent', { ns: '' })`, `w.tell('@p1 pet owner=$e.user name=rex')` in `ns: 'A'` is `dangling-ref $A::e.user`; `owner=$::e.user` works. It should fall back to the default namespace for shared types. (The host writes `$::e.user`: `toLib`.)
  6. Untested but read in the source: `check(patch, { query })` runs the inner query with `{}` (no `ns`), so a `where` reference in it is not qualified.
- **Host findings from the warnings.** `unknown-attribute template.item` on `tasks.a.add` (the host reads `template.<key>`, expected) and `card=many` on `gs.k.lt` / `gs.k.lx` of `games.guess` (the library reads `many=true`; the slots are therefore single-valued today; left as it is so that behaviour stays identical; worth a decision).
- **Not done / honest limits.** `shared=true` for `core.agent` has no effect until item 3 (the instances are single-namespace, so nothing depends on it); `docs.editor` is the one instance in the default namespace (item 2); there is no per-turn namespace: facts of different turns must join (a count over purchases, a fluent over events), and a namespace per turn broke every aggregate and every reference to an agent in a trial (answers: "I don't know how much money you have"); the turn goes in the ids instead.

## REGRESSION-AB (2026-11-12): matrix no longer worse than ops in the dialogues

- **Result.** `ab-sopworld --sets coherence,dialogues,gold` (803 sessions, `training/results/sopworld-ab-2026-11-12.json`, classes in `.classes.json`): 0 "ops better" (7 before), 11 matrix better, 15 neutral wording, 0 unjudged (the 8 unjudged dialogues and one gold session are classified with notes). One open question in the classes file: dlg.avt#011, an undo of "Yes" (become the emoji) goes back to the library state before it, which still holds the open offer (`ui.avatar.pending`); ops forgets the offer.
- **Chess (gms#002, gms#006, doc#035): a real bug, fixed.** Two causes. (1) The engine's late reply ("Meanwhile I play knight to c6.") was told inside the user's next turn, so one timeline step held both plies. A world now says it with `ctx.checkpoint(text)` (ops) or `live.checkpoint(text)` (fns): the host adopts what the world has so far and begins the user's step after it (`ReasonerSession.checkpoint`); an action cannot mark inside its transaction (the library throws "committed to a state shared with a fork"), so the fn commits, stops, and `resolve` marks and runs it again with `live.carry` as the first words. (2) "Make your move." (the wait counter) was a step of its own, so the engine's reply of the next turn was rewound with it and the undo stopped one ply early. `adopt` may now return `quiet: true` (games.chess: only the transient rest moved): no step. Engine replies that arrive as observations were already outside every turn. (3) doc#035: a generic undo did not note its turn for "what did you do?"; `discourse.noteWorld` now does, as the world's own undo does.
- **The four "same reply, worse outcome": a view difference, not a told fact (decision (b)).** kidsA#010: "Zoe eats 8. How many marbles are left?" is half understood; "Zoe ate 8 marbles" is told in BOTH modes (turn 3 says 11 in both), matrix only shows it in `kids.arith.holdings` (spec 15 `toState`); ops keeps it in wires. The judge compared the whole state, so the not-understood part was "wrong" in matrix, "not understood" in ops. drm#011/014/021: art.draw's matrix view had no `history`/`future` and a refused turn made the empty lists appear (the ops operations create them), so the key set changed on a turn that changed nothing. Fix: art.draw's `toState` keeps `history: []`, `future: []` (the view no longer changes shape), and the judges (`scripts/lib/visible-state.mjs`, used by ab-sopworld and the eval-* scripts) compare the state without `ui.help` and `kids.arith.holdings`. Nothing is told on a not-understood turn in either mode.
- **Gate.** `tests/ab-gate.test.mjs` runs `ab-sopworld --sets dialogues --ids <17 dialogues, the seven among them> --no-write` and fails on any "ops better" (6 s). `tests/regression-ab.test.mjs`: the three chess dialogues in both modes, a second undo, and the observation path. Chrome: `chess-late` block in `scripts/test-webchat-matrix.mjs` (race-tolerant rows).
- **Gates run.** `npm test`, `test-world all` (both reasoners), `build-webchat.mjs`, `test-webchat-matrix.mjs` 186/186, `test:browser` (see the report).

## 2026-11-12 geomap intermittent (map tab echoing its view)
- Cause: docs/webchat/ui/tabs/map.mjs reported its view (zoom/center) to the world 350 ms after every `moveend`, including the moves the world itself asked for (setMaxZoom clamp on the offline layer, animated flyTo). `host.setWorldState` puts that into the session state and the library `adopt`s it at the next operation as a user change (a turn that clears the redo steps, a new undo step): a fractional intermediate zoom (14.75) reached the state, and a late report landed between undo and redo so that redo did not restore the offline layer.
- Fix (product): a guard (`programmatic`) suppresses reports while apply() changes the layer or flies; apply() cancels a pending report; and a report equal to the state the world set (zoom, center, no bounds) is dropped as an echo. A clamp, undo and redo of the library now win. No unit test: the race is in the Leaflet tab (browser only); the Node side (adopt of a host patch) is by design.
- Other tabs: data.charts, art.draw, diagram.sketch do not call host.setWorldState (they only send commands), so they have no echo path; docs.editor (selection/cursor on user click only), docs.reader (visible flag, asserted once), media.music (playing=false on end) report on user events only.
- Gates: geomap 14/14 under 14 parallel throttled Chrome runs (before: about 1 in 12 failed), full matrix and npm test, see commit.

The one unread: the fragment "a bigger table 1" (dialogue module).
**Risks and findings for the reviewer.**
1. The engine's discourse layer owns "redo" and cancels it on any later turn (a query between undo and redo ends it). The executor's own redo works only when a host calls it directly. Same for every tab world today; a candidate engine fix: do not clear the redo stack on a read-only turn.
2. The engine rewrote the pronoun in "why is it blue" to "why is blue blue" (some referent substitution before the patterns); the why-answer falls back to the focus when no thing is named. Cause not found in this session.
3. Lexicons of attribute / value words must not be `class=noun` (the engine takes the last noun for "it"); the generator uses `modifier`.

**1. Bundled default face = data.** `scripts/build-default-face.mjs` now keeps every slot (16, with the catalog's aliases: eyeglasses, specs, cap, mustache ...), EVERY preset (14: boy, man, robot ...) and every expression (angry, sad ...), the four colours, and for each slot every variant that a preset or expression names, else its first (48 kB, was 13 kB). **2. The act belongs to the open tab (general rule, `_tabOwnsAct` in src/dialog/index.mjs, both reasoners).** Cause: "remove the hat" had no reading in ui.avatar (no bare "remove" pattern), so art.draw's `remove {words}` (tier 5, no competitor) answered "I can't find the hat in the picture". Rule: a reading of a world the message does not name, whose act (last word of its action) is also an action of the world on the open tab, whose dry run finds nothing to act on / refuses, and that no other reading replaces, moves to the tab world's pattern for that act, arguments by shape (one text argument to one text argument); the tab world answers in its own words. It does not fire when the foreign pattern has words of its own beside the act ("remove milk from my LIST") or a slot of its lexicon (a thing of that world is named): kids.tasks tests n8 and n55 showed that first. Result: "remove the hat" -> "I took off a bow hat.", "remove eyeglasses" -> "I have no glasses already.", "remove the unicorn" -> "I have nothing like unicorn on my face". Side effect found by test-world: a FRESH session's default tab is the Avatar ("robot"), so art.draw test err01 ("Delete the car." on an empty picture) now needs `given="ui.shell:activeTab=draw"` (done); every other world passes in both reasoners (only the known ledger row media.music.sh04 fails).

New invariant in tests/invariants.test.mjs (both reasoners): over the English owner-log messages plus remove/delete probes on four tabs, no refusal (`unsupported` / `missing`) comes from a world that is not the tab's, is not named in the message, for an act the tab's world has. Checked that it FAILS without the rule (5 hits on the Avatar tab) and passes with it. Wider finding for the ledger (not fixed, by the rule): the same sweep without the "act of the tab" condition shows ~40 owner-log turns answered by a refusal of another world (single letters "a", "e" on the Hangman tab answered "We are not playing hangman" by games.hangman, "why?" answered by games.guess, "draw ..." on the Charts tab by data.charts); they are one class, "wrong world answers with a refusal", for the analysis script.

Agreement with dispatcher + patterns on the operational + dialogue sets (the rules' act read by verb from the winning request action; 748 messages comparable, 443 in the doing worlds): DistilBERT 80.6 %, 6x384 76.1 %, 4x384 77.0 %; single-command messages of the doing worlds (362): 86.7 / 81.8 / 81.8 %. A lower bound: the action -> act mapping is a heuristic, the tagger sees no tab or history, and compound messages are one input.

Findings: (1) all three transfer to the unseen worlds on act (98.8 to 99.1 %) and on role spans except thing / set (held-out span F1 95.4 / 95.1 / 94.0 against 99.8 / 99.7 / 99.7 on seen worlds: gap 4.4 / 4.6 / 5.8 points, within 5 for the first two). (2) The generated sets are easy, so the table separates the sizes by cost, not accuracy: 6x384 is 2.9x smaller and 3.4x faster than DistilBERT for 0.25 points of held-out span F1; the 4-layer model 3.5x smaller and 5.8x faster for 1.4 points. (3) Cold load at 1 MB/s is what moves: 67 s against 23 s and 19 s (creating the graph at 4x is 1.1 to 1.3 s for all). (4) On real messages the tagger needs the logs: compound messages, follow-ups and a none / question class are not in the label set. Cause: on the default tab (the Avatar) the avatar's forms are tier 3 whatever other world reads the sentence, so every form with a free slot (save / "write down", "who are you", "my name is", "is a square a rectangle", place.dir) captured sentences of kids.common, kids.shapes, docs.editor, user.profile, kids.tasks, media.music, tictactoe, art.draw: 34 failing test-world cases. General fixes: (1) the formalizer's decline gets the segment text, the tab and `claim`, and a world's catch-all reading (free text slots) is dropped when another world has a reading with no free text at all, unless the world holds the focus of the dialogue (lastWorld) or says so (`accepts` returns 'focus'); (2) tabClaim only when the sentence itself says yourself / your / the avatar / the face; (3) `save` only with a face word or "save this/it as"; place / remove / ask need every word to be a face word; (4) `who are you` is not an avatar form; (5) a fallback by `outOfScope` needs a thing of the world (an act verb alone, "Add please", is the engine's not understood). Result: `test-world all` in both reasoners 33 worlds, 0 failing cases (ui.avatar 18/18, plan.seating 7/7, art.draw 596/596 ops and 600/600 matrix); the avatar-related test files: 4 not ok left, all marked todo or the old canonical-examples (talk) failures; tests/acts, pilot-avatar, things, dialogue, bounded-captures, rd10 green; smoke 16 s. (2) The drawing board is bridged without being a view: its referents (`ctx.sessionFacts()`, new hook next to `ctx.dialogueFocus`, also set on the dry-run fork, or every such request is judged "missing" in the dry run) enter the store. (3) `data.charts` and `docs.editor` are views through a `view` and an `adopt` operation (26 and 45 hand-written lines of ops, plus 4 operation/template entries each). (4) `doc.make`: the act make-document with a title and content in one request (18 lines, 2 patterns, test in tests.sop). (5) M1 `sessionContent` and its `factsList` / `factsProse` are deleted (about 45 lines of dialogue.mjs); the dialogue test keeps the facts check, the chart/document behaviour is in tests/things.test.mjs. (6) `worlds/plan.timeline`: a view from a schema alone (52 lines of schema.sop, everything else generated, 30 lines of tab plugin, `tabOnly=yes`), things with a temporal aspect (`k.time`) are taken as moments even when the schema has no word for their kind (adopt: a kind the world declares with an aspect the thing has).
**T1 matrix, 5 views + timeline (both reasoners identical; 3 views alone were 60 cells 22 right / 38 not applicable / 0 wrong).** 34 things (30 + 4 calendar things from Talk) made in the avatar, the seating plan and Talk, each sent to every other view: 170 cells, 89 right, 76 not applicable said plainly, 5 wrong. By target: talk 20/0/0, seating 1/23/0, avatar 1/23/0, chart 29/0/5, document 34/0/0, timeline 4/30/0 (right / not applicable / wrong). The 5 wrong are one class: "send table N to the chart" (a number in the sentence) is read by the chart's own data pattern (`r2.create.data.trail`, the named-world tier of routing) before the seating plan's send; not patched, in the ledger class below. With `--draw` (pilot art.draw as the fourth view): 264 cells, 119 / 123 / 22; the extra 17 wrong are the existing talk/avatar to draw cells (12 on main before this work) plus the 4 calendar things. T2 is unchanged (40 cells 8 right / 26 not applicable / 6 wrong, same as before). Chart and document are columns only: they publish no things of their own yet, so no row is made in them (limit in the spec).
**Hand-written lines outside schema + renderer + own rules, per world:** talk: 0 new (its send branches target draw / diagram / map, none target charts or the editor; unchanged, goes when those are views); data.charts: 26 ops + 12 sop (operations) + 8 (templates); docs.editor: 63 ops (make 16, view+adopt 47) + 19 sop (patterns) + 18 + 12; plan.timeline: 0 lines of code (schema 52, world 17, legend 6, tests 19; tab plugin 30); session.things (shared, once for all pairs): select 35 + bridge/show 48 lines, 3 patterns, 2 lexicons. Replaced per-pair code: M1 sessionContent (dialogue.mjs, about 45 lines).
**Checks.** test-world all, both reasoners: the one failure of main (media.music sh04), nothing added. Targeted: tests/things.test.mjs 11/11 (2 new), tests/dialogue.test.mjs unchanged failure (a fragment with a place, fails on main too). Smoke once: green except "the built webchat is fresh" (docs/webchat not rebuilt here: the reviewer rebuilds after merging). Found on the way and fixed as general causes: the dry run (`forkForValidation`) had no session facts, so every "chart of the discussion" read was rejected as missing; the view words must be a lexicon or "number of items on my list" is read as a request for a view (test-world caught it: kids.tasks sw122).

## 2026-11-13 TRANSFER: the map as a view, a send that names a view, T3 rule transfer (common sense at the knowledge tier)
**What changed (general mechanisms, no code per pair).** (1) `geo.map` is a view of the session things (`geo.map.view` / `.adopt`, geographic aspect, many): pins for what the map can place (name, kind, or `lat` / `lon`), plain words for the rest; selection phrases "show it on the map" and "put the places we talked about on the map" (patterns of `session.things`; the noun names an aspect: `ASPECT_NOUN_TEMPORARY`); Talk's per-pair `send` branch to the map, its pattern `pat.talk.send.map` and the phrase `lang.talk.tomap` are deleted (the map is reached by `things.show`). (3) T3: `src/knowledge/commonsense.mjs` is the one lookup of where a kind usually is (`k.scenes` place, `k.commonsense` at, taught or catalog, the kind-of chain); Talk's answer uses it for every kind (it was only for taught ones), the drawing board asks it for a kind with no row of its own (default place fallback, and the advice in both reasoners through `ctx.rulesAdvise`, a flag added to the operation context so a kind is never advised twice), `parseTeach` reads "a house stands on the ground" and the other habitat verbs. `scripts/exp-transfer.mjs` got T3 (`--only t3`, `--ledger` appends the wrong cells to `training/eval/failures.jsonl`) and a map column in T1.

Talk 9 -> 19 of 20; drawing 7 -> 8 right of 15 that apply (the real board, no pilot); diagram 0 of 11. T1 with the map as a seventh column: 204 cells, 97 right, 107 not applicable said plainly, 0 wrong (the 5 wrong chart cells of the last entry are the send class of (2)); map column 3 right (Paris, France, Japan from Talk) / 31 na. T2 unchanged against HEAD (8 right / 23 na / 9 wrong in the 40 other-view cells with the pilot board on the path; I ran HEAD in a scratch copy to check; the 9 are the pilot drawing taking "put on a cottage" and "seat the dogs", and the ones already in the last entry).
**T3 ledger (38 rows: 19 per reasoner, `cause` field), by cause.** diagram has no place semantics, nothing asks the knowledge tier (11 per reasoner): a connection is an arrow with no meaning, so there is nothing to refuse or label; the fix is a view with a spatial / containment relation, not a patch; the drawing grammar does not read "<kind> in the <place>" for a kind of the catalog or a taught kind (4: lighthouse, snowman, train, plane: "I did not understand ... Draw the sky"); "in the water" is read as the bottom band and the place word is lost (3: sun, cloud, car); another world (kids.animals) reads "ducks float" first and keeps the fact private (1). ## 2026-11-13 diagram switch (branch diagram-switch, worker)
worlds/diagram.sketch is the generated schema world (schema.sop + hooks.mjs + own.mjs; the engine wrapper is now engine.mjs, imports updated; the legend words of the old lexicon are kept as lexicon.extra.sop that the generator appends). Old patterns, operations, templates, fns.mjs, matrix.sop, matrix.templates.sop removed; reasoner=ops (no native matrix: the leftovers made six other worlds fail in the matrix reasoner). General mechanisms added: (1) frame forms `read.frame*` (non-tab, priority 30): a sentence that names the diagram or says "box/chart shaped like X" / "a shape in the form of X" is the diagram's whatever the tab, `accepts` returns 'focus', the drawing board never sees it; (2) connect after "and": the pronoun is replaced by the last thing only for the connect act, not for a whole "add ... and connect A to it" sentence (the engine reads it whole); (3) splitClauses keeps a comma after a rule frame ("from now on," "by default,") inside the sentence; (4) schema keys `tabUndo` (undo/redo forms tab only), `claim` (tabClaim on every form), `signal` (router signal), `boost` (priority bonus), `accepts` outside the tab declines unless the sentence names the diagram, a shape of it, named shapes or arrows; (5) `{x:words}` instead of rest for leading slots (rest runs to the end). tests/acts.test.mjs allows the role `post`.
Result: tests.sop of the old world 759 -> 758 of 771 in both reasoners after the final regeneration (today 771); the 13 rows that fail are in training/eval/failures.jsonl (class + cause, was_passing true): arrange/snap/group/align with name lists cut at commas (4), refusal wordings of the old world (ask_path.k02, group.k02), no-tab cases (create.k06, delete.k04, ex.star.n001), disconnect read as delete, "Nudge" read by kids.tasks, "from now on rectangles are tiny" without comma, undo wording. test-world all in both reasoners: 34 worlds, only those 13 rows fail. Node tests (diagram, arrows, acts, things, undo-redo) 84 pass; smoke 17.7 s green.

## 2026-11-13 sopworld 0.23.0 vendored; switch to shared things / taught tier / catalog: NOT done, why, and the plan (worker)
Vendored (commit 09caa09c): `src/vendor/sopworld/sopworld.mjs` 0.23.0 (build 2c7044be7436, 527910 bytes, sha256 in `src/vendor/LICENSES.md`, pinned at library commit 8b763ad), plus `tools/build-bundle.mjs` and the one module it imports (`src/knowledge.mjs`) byte for byte, so `node src/vendor/sopworld/tools/build-bundle.mjs <catalog dir> <out.json> <word|shard|world> ...` runs unmodified (probed on a copy of `knowledge/k.objects`: 2 files, loads into a World with `createCatalog` + `bundleReader`, `intoSync` ok). Vendor test updated, webchat rebuilt. Checks: `tests/reasoner.test.mjs` 54/54; `test-world all` 0 failures with `--reasoner ops` and `--reasoner matrix`. Lines deleted: 0.

Why the "thin adapters, then delete ours" step was not done: the library's pieces and ours are not the same shape, and the replacement is a rewrite of the consumers, not an adapter.
1. `createCatalog` / `bundleReader` TELL shards (schemas first) into a `World`; they return paths and violations. Our `src/knowledge/facts.mjs` (295 lines) returns JS records: `peek` / `thing` (senses, objects, commonsense, drawnAs, wires), `wires(type, {key, shard})`, `schema()`, `series()`, `faces()`, `countOf`, `unreachable()`, the retry-after-outage logic and the compute-budget ticks. About 25 consumers (`knowledge-lookup.mjs`, art.draw, avatar, talk, geo, the dialogue fill tiers, exp-transfer) read those records synchronously (`ctx.knowledge.peek`). Replacing it means answering the same questions from wires in a World (queries) and re-proving T1/T2/T3, Talk E-T1 and knowledge-lookup: a task of its own, and `facts.mjs` is being edited by KNOWLEDGE-OUT right now (merge conflict, and numbers that move for another reason).
2. `teach` / `forget` take a SOP wire and tell it at the tier `taught` in a World with `std.know`. Our `learn()` (12 lines) is only the store; the 140 lines of `learned.mjs` are the English forms (`parseTeach`) and the overlay (`withLearned`: senses, is-a chain to a drawing, owner things, `ancestors`, session-memory records). The English reading stays host glue either way. The overlay can go only when the consumers read facts + `taught` wires from a World, which is point 1 again.
3. Shared things / aspects / views / `show` live in ONE `World` whose things are made by acts (`make`). `worlds/session.things` is a registry over the items of tab worlds that run in our interpreter (`sync` of each tab's item list, `viewsOf` by the tabs' `view` operation, `adopt` per tab). Moving to the library's things means the tabs' items become wires of a std.schema world (art.draw, seating, timeline, docs, charts, geo all create their items in their own state today). That is the "tab worlds become schema worlds" migration (P1 pilot: ui.avatar and diagram.sketch in `worlds-pilot/`), not a swap of session.things.
Proposed order (smallest first, each measured on T1/T2/T3 + Talk E-T1 + knowledge-lookup before the next): (a) after KNOWLEDGE-OUT lands, one session World per session with `std.know`; `learn()` also tells the wire there with `teach` (both stores agree, a test compares them), then `withLearned` reads its wires from the World and the line store goes; (b) `facts.mjs` `wires()` / `schema()` / `series()` answered from catalog-told wires (`createCatalog.into`) while `thing()` keeps the record shape as a view over them; (c) tab worlds to schema worlds one by one (art.draw first: 7 own types, the selection / last-thing rules go to the library), `session.things.sync` shrinks to nothing as the last tab moves. Estimated deletion when all three are done: learned.mjs about 150 of 178, session.things ops/things/view about 400 of 462, facts.mjs wires/schema/series/loading about 150 of 295.

Next migration list from the library's reuse report (`docs/reuse-reports/psys2.md`, sopworld at 4938e83; 157 candidates, top 20: 8 believed): (1) the selection and last-thing rules repeated in art.draw (`ad.d.sel`, `ad.d.last`), diagram.sketch (`dk.d.last`), docs.editor (`ed.d.sel`), docs.reader: "a selection must name a thing that exists", one shared check (score 1.00); (2) orphan-reference denies (art.draw `ad.d.nokind`, data.charts `dc.d.orphan`, docs.editor `ed.d.none`) and no-two-with-the-same-name (`ad.d.twice`, `dk.d.name`, `dk.d.sid`: already `core.type unique=`); (3) the lookup actions of kids.animals (7: canFly/canSwim ...), kids.shapes (describeShape, colorOf), kids.time (monthDays): one generic `ask` act over knowledge (verdict: partly, not a shared module); (4) chess / tic-tac-toe `game` and `move` types (shape 0.80 / 0.75) as one game / move module; (5) `art.draw.tally` ~ `docs.editor.want`: the aggregate is shared, the meaning is not (partly). Reuse number 0 for most worlds (only chess 0.88, media.music 0.82, plan.seating 1.0 reuse from elsewhere).

## 2026-11-14 smoke invariants after the art.draw switch (agent task "fix invariants first")
**Result: smoke exits 0.** Four invariant groups were red; three were real bugs of shared code, one was never the network.
- **Network (`network-never-changes-reading`):** not a network bug. The readings and replies with a rejected or hanging catalog were already equal to those of no catalog (the `deepEqual` passed); the failing assertion was `show Pariss` on the map tab answered Paris. The cause: the generated `pat.art.draw.ask.options.verb` (`show {thing:words}`) took any free words, and the draw `accepts` hook accepted every `ask options`, so the Drawing world read "show Pariss" as "list what I can draw" before the tab's typo repair. Fix in `worlds/art.draw/hooks.mjs`: an `ask options` reading is the drawing's only when its free words name the drawing (a kind of the catalog, a colour or shade word, "things", "options", "draw" ...). Spelling and the open-class lookups were not touched.
- **Destructive clause next to a clause that is not understood:** nothing ran, but the reply did not name the part that was read ("clear everything and zork the plimp" is one clause for the acts reader: the thing role is a coordination, `fork the plimp` has no referent, the world-aware veto fires). `heldPart` in `src/dialog/world-aware.mjs`: when the missing name follows a connector inside one clause, the reply adds `I did not act on "<the earlier part>" either, because I could not read all of your message.` The hold itself (one vetoed clause holds the readable ones) already applied; this is the same sentence for a coordination inside one clause.
- **Undo, one step per request (spec 15, owner rule 2026-11-13):** the acts executor collapsed every history entry of a turn into the first (`stepGroup` + `done`, spec 21 "one undo step per message"), and `add` of art.draw merged "and a tree" into the step of the first thing (`history.splice(-2, 1)`). Both removed: a request (one thing of a coordination, one wire of a message) is one history entry; only an explicit act group (`actGroup`, ids `grpN_`) stays one step. Two more gaps of the matrix path for a world that keeps its own history: `_redo` sent "redo" to the generic timeline whenever a matrix session existed (now the world's own redo answers unless the undo was a step of the timeline), and `_undoNamed` returned null when the timeline had steps but not the named one (now it falls through to the actions list, as without a timeline).
- **Tests changed:** `tests/undo-redo.test.mjs` "the timeline entries of a message share its turn" now uses the shop (a library world); the drawing is not on the matrix timeline since the switch. `tests/known-failures.json`: 11 entries removed (2 network, 7 undo-redo, 2 destructive clause) because they pass; the 2 left in smoke are the arbitration ones (`the world that answers is the world of the open tab`, ops and matrix: `remove the unicorn` on the robot and draw tabs goes to kids.tasks), owned by the arbitration task.
- **Measure:** smoke exits 0 (2 known, both arbitration); `undo-redo` 25/25, `network-never-changes-reading` 2/2, `invariants` 8 of 10 standalone (the 2 arbitration; "no message changes the tab" passes under the runner); test-world all failing rows: ops 62 (main 63), matrix 67 (main 71), no world got worse (geo.map back to complete).

## 2026-11-14 BOOT-CACHE: the 5-minute "Loading the worlds", one manifest, a service worker, one popup (reviewer 05:30 items 1-4, 05:10 items 6-7)
**The 5-minute load (item 1).** Reproduced cold at 1 MB/s (page, engine worker and service worker all throttled) and with a stale cache of an older build (5181fac0 then the current one): the chat is usable after 3 to 13 s, but the panel said "Loading the worlds" for ever (110 s of probe: the label never changed, not even while the 65 MB reading model downloaded behind it). Cause: the engine worker's `boot-step` events (start and end of `worlds` and `reasoner`), added in db6781c1, had been lost when the worlds fetch moved into the worker; nothing ended those steps and the panel showed the first active step of the plan as long as the page lived. No loop on the unreachable catalog, no stale-index loop; the real waits are the 4.6 MB `worlds/index.json` (7 s at 1 MB/s) and the 65 MB model (70 to 90 s). Fix: the worker reports the steps again, the page ends whatever is left after the boot; tests: `tests/webchat-assets.test.mjs` (source check) and `scripts/test-webchat-boot.mjs` cold ("no start-up step stays open"). A user whose browser holds the old `index.html` (GitHub Pages `max-age=600`) keeps the old stuck page for up to ten minutes after the deploy; nothing in new code can reach that page.
**Policy (items 2, 3).** `build-info.json` is the manifest: `version` plus `assets` (a hash for each of the 364 files; modules keep the graph version their URL carries; `style.css` and `favicon.svg` links are stamped); `index.html` stamps the version. New `docs/webchat/sw.js` caches every asset forever under `path?v=hash`, shares concurrent fetches, deletes entries not in the manifest on every new manifest, revalidates only `index.html`, leaves `models/**` to their own sha256 caches. New `docs/webchat/ui/assets.mjs`: release reset (once per `CACHE_GENERATION` = 1: Cache Storage, service workers, IndexedDB, `psys2.webchat.progress`, `psys2.ortlog`; settings, history and every other key kept), the manifest fetched once with no cache, a stale page reloads once and says "A new version is available. Reloading once…" (session guard, no loop; the old banner only when still stale after one reload), the page posts the manifest to the service worker. Catalog shards stay cached by the catalog `version` (knowledge-cache.mjs, unchanged).
**One fetch (item 4).** The "early" fetches of index.html (worlds/index.json, dispatcher meta.json) were never read; the page now reads them and hands the worlds bytes to the worker (`worldsBytes`, also on a restart) and the meta object to `findDispatcherModel`; About reads the manifest of this start. Tests count at the server: no file twice per start, every request hashed except index.html, build-info.json, sw.js and `models/**`, a warm start sees only index.html, build-info.json, the models' meta.json and sw.js (5 requests, 33 KB), Cache Storage has one entry per path and every entry in the manifest, an update leaves exactly the new build (`scripts/test-webchat-boot.mjs` cold / warm / update / reset, `tests/webchat-boot.test.mjs`; `tests/webchat-assets.test.mjs` is in the smoke list).
**The popup (item 5).** `ui/progress.mjs`: the latest running step only in plain words ("Loading the reading model (12 of 65 MB)…"), no count, no "Ready", note and Details only in developer mode, a step shows only after 0.7 s (a start from the cache shows nothing), `quiet` steps (voices) never show, `immediate` for the update message; failures keep their notice with Dismiss.
**Romanian model errors (05:10 item 7).** Not reproducible on an English start: no Romanian file requested on a cold or a warm profile, with the fake browser Translator API or without. The page did fetch the registry and ask the browser's Translator about every registry pair (about 60 questions) at every start; English now loads the registry only (`init({ probe: false })`) and nothing else until a language is picked or Settings is opened. Romanian model requests (storage.googleapis.com, cross-origin) happen when the saved language is Romanian; an old saved "auto" migrates to the browser language. To see the failing file in the owner's browser: Settings > Language, and the Details fold in developer mode.
**Measures (1 MB/s on page, workers and service worker; headless Chrome; default settings, so the 65 MB reading model downloads; first 25 s counted at the server).** Cold, before / after: requests in the first 25 s 284 / 287, bytes 14.5 / 14.5 MB (the model streams; the whole start 97.5 MB both); chat usable 12.9 s / 13.2 s; the panel said "Loading the worlds" until the end / showed worlds (3.8 s), reasoner (8.3 s), face set, runtime, "Loading the reading model (n of 65 MB)" and was hidden at 103 s when the model was ready. Warm (everything cached): 5 requests, 15 KB / 6 requests, 33 KB (index.html and build-info.json revalidations, the models' meta.json, sw.js), chat usable 1.0 s / 1.2 to 2.7 s, panel stuck on "Loading the worlds" / no popup at all. Start-up table (step, ms, bytes) of the new cold start: page 2,532 ms 1.86 MB; worlds 5,319 ms 4.59 MB; reasoner 4,541 ms; model 89,272 ms 65 MB; translator 0; catalog failed (probe has no route to the catalog); voices 2,500 (quiet); map data 2,592; faces 6,033. Warm: page 366, worlds 472, reasoner 835, model 570, voices 2,500 (quiet), map data 315, faces 339. The size of a cold start did not change on purpose: lazy world loading and the compact index are the next task.
**Tests run:** `tests/webchat-assets.test.mjs` (7), `tests/webchat-progress-log.test.mjs`, `tests/webchat-build.test.mjs`, `tests/build-versioning.test.mjs`, `scripts/test-webchat-boot.mjs` (30/30), `scripts/test-webchat-version.mjs`, `scripts/test-webchat-phone.mjs` (all), `scripts/test-webchat-language.mjs` (55/55), `scripts/test-webchat-ui.mjs` (55/55), smoke. `tests/webchat-settings.test.mjs` "an explicit later choice of rules" fails on the unchanged tree too (settings.mjs not touched here). ## 2026-11-14 loading failures on the published phone ("Something did not load": Romanian model and picture catalog)
- **Reproduced** (headless Chrome, Pixel UA, 412x915 touch, saved language `ro`, published page): `Failed to fetch` for all six Romanian model files, console "blocked by CORS policy". Cause 1: Mozilla's Google bucket (`storage.googleapis.com/moz-fx-translations-data...`) returns `access-control-allow-origin` for `http://localhost:*` only (curl with `Origin:` of the Pages site, example.com: no header, also on the OPTIONS preflight). Every run from a real origin fails; our local tests ran on localhost and never saw it. The service worker is not involved (cross-origin requests are not intercepted). The Mozilla Remote Settings CDN has CORS `*` but answers 406 to a Chrome User-Agent: no way out there.
- Cause 2 (catalog): `app.mjs` calls `engineClient.call('catalog')` at the end of start-up, and `engine-worker.mjs` had no `catalog` op ("unknown op catalog"), so the step always failed: "The picture catalog could not be reached" on every start, with the catalog answering 200. Second, smaller cause: `index.json`/`vocab.json` (about 200 kB gzip each) had the same 6 s bound as a shard, too short for a 50 kB/s phone, and an unreachable catalog was never asked again.
- **Fix.** Romanian model files are mirrored under `docs/webchat/models-mt/ro/` (29 MB, `scripts/mirror-mt-models.mjs`, `mirror` per file in the registry) and read first from the page host, then from the bucket; each URL is tried twice; failed model downloads retry by themselves (4/15/45 s), then one plain popup with "Try again" (`progress.fail(..., { retry })`, `progress.resolve(id)` clears it). Worker op `catalog` (reads the vocabulary, `{ ok, bytes }`, `refresh` skips the backoff via `facts.refresh()`); the page retries it (4/12/30 s, then every minute) and clears the notice; bounds 25 s for index/vocab, 8 s for shards. Saved language Romanian on the owner's phone is expected (the model loads for `ro`; for `en` nothing is downloaded). Other languages are still bucket-only: they work on localhost only until mirrored (run the mirror script for them; about 25 to 100 MB each).
- Verified: `tests/webchat-loading-failures.test.mjs` (op-exists check over the page and the worker, registry mirror files match, download order and failure, refresh, resolve); local build on 127.0.0.1 (a CORS-blocked origin for the bucket) with mobile emulation, Fast 3G: all six files from `models-mt/`, progress 14 of 30 MB, no popup; unthrottled: no failure notice. `npm run test:smoke`: see the commit.

## 2026-11-14 LAZY-LOAD-2: residuals of the lazy-loading landing, fixed at the cause (undo after reload, 4 UI checks, the 1.7 % readings, the Romanian migration, the Settings switch)
**1. Undo after a reload (invariant: undo per request).** Cause: `engine.reload` makes a new session and the worker did `snaps.clear()`, so an undo of an earlier turn went through the page's state record (state and memory only). Fix: `DialogSession.portableSnapshot(snap)` turns each kept snapshot into plain data before the reload (the session is put back), `adoptSnapshot(rec)` makes a snapshot of the new session out of it (the old state laid over the new session's states, the memory with the undo timeline). Before: draw, a message that loads a world, undo of the drawing turn: the snapshot was gone. After: `tests/lazy-loading.test.mjs` "UNDO AFTER A RELOAD" (the page-level snapshot of the drawing turn takes the drawing back; the chat "undo" after "How many legs does a spider have?", which loads worlds, takes the drawing back).
**2. The four UI checks.** Three causes, none a missing await of the tab module. (a) Header line (desktop and phone): the avatar's head icon is a `span.p2-head-face` created at boot (its world is the open tab's), the test read the first `span`; the test now excludes it. (b) "give me an example command" and "Start a new page" (the die and the chips): the page set the open tab (`setWorldState ui.shell activeTab`) and the engine said "You are on the Charts tab": `restoreMemory` replays the matrix reasoner's timeline (`rs.restoreJSON`), which DERIVES a matrix world's state from instances that never heard of host patches, so every restore (a reload for a world, a restart) put the old tab, and any other host-set state, back. `restoreMemory` now keeps the world states in place across the replay. Also: `ensureRun` read the state BEFORE its awaits, so a click during the load was lost; it reads after the last await and builds the new session with no await between. (c) "Stop ends dictation" (same cause: the editor's mode state is host-set). Before: 4 checks failing (header phone and desktop, Stop phone and desktop; the chips as above). After: `--only ui1,doc,surprise`: header, Stop, "example command", tab switches all pass; what remains in the 50 clicks is the offline catalog (dolphins, "7 plus 5" colour and number words), the same on main in this sandbox (main `--only surprise`: 3 failing checks of 20 with different random chips). `--only settings` on main fails the 4 helper-model checks and the history-list height with or without this change (not mine).
**3. The 1.7 % readings that look complete and differ.** `scripts/eval-word-index.mjs --designs B --T 2 --nospell`, now 1,818 messages (the corpus grew), WI_DEBUG lists every difference with the worlds, effects and changed states. Before: 35 differences (1.9 %) among the readings not read again. Classes and fixes: (a) 24 of 35: an ACTION nobody had loaded (kids.common asks `prof.setName` of user.profile; "I want to play hangman" got "no operation for action 'hm.new'"; tic tac toe, twenty questions; talk asks `draw.add`): the interpreter records an unresolved action (`session.takeMissed()`), `index.actions` maps the actions of the worlds that are not always loaded to their world, the worker loads that world and reads the turn again. (b) 3: "what can you do", "what commands do you recognise": the help world lists the loaded worlds, so a help turn that called `ctx.worlds()` loads every world. (c) 8: a SWALLOW: a free-text slot of three words or more that holds a joiner or a question word ("what is the capital of Japan then how many days are in a week": the map world took the second request as the name of a thing; the clause cutter only cuts what the uncut reading left unread): `readingIncomplete` (in `src/worlds/word-index.mjs`, one function for the worker, the eval script and the test harness) calls it not complete. After: 6 differences (0.33 %): two are an artefact of the eval (a process-wide task id counter: `task_159` against `task_3`), four are one documented class: a loaded world and an unloaded one both read the whole message and the unloaded one wins by routing ("make it bigger twice", "go back", "and the day after that", "draw a nice chart about the current discussion"; no word names it; only loading it can tell). Cost: 996 of 1,818 messages are read a second time (919 before, +77; 55 % against 50 %), the extra loaded worlds per message 2.55 and 0.97 false positives are the index's, unchanged. Spec 06 "Lazy loading" says so.
**4. The Romanian mid-session difference.** Cause: the same as the missing initial states: `restoreStates` put the old, partial state IN PLACE of the new session's, so every world loaded by the reload (talk, user.profile, data.charts, ...) had no initial state; plus the tab/shell state above. A node probe (`ro-matrix-sessions.json`, rules translator, English start, switch to Romanian, reload at the first message, every turn compared on text and the whole state with a full start): 22 turns differed in state before (text equal); 0 after (the old state is laid over the new session's: `{...fresh, ...old}`; test "a world loaded later has its initial state"). The phone path through the machine-translation model cannot run here (the model is not available offline); the rules path is proved. A session that starts in Romanian still loads every world at start.
**5. Settings.** Developer > Experiments > "Load worlds when a message needs them" (`lazyWorlds`, default on, restarts the engine; the worker reads `m.settings.lazyWorlds` or the boot flag `?psys2lazy=0`), with its numbers and date (start 5.8 s against 13.3 s, 0.57 MB against 4.6 MB of worlds; replies the same).
**Tests run.** `tests/lazy-loading.test.mjs` 9 tests (4 new: undo after reload, initial state of a late world, state set during a load, the corpus of ten messages now includes the swallow, the hangman start and the help list); undo-redo, live-state, settings-coherent, discourse-memory, reasoner-restore (its "40-turn session" test fails on main too: a direct `rs.restoreJSON` call, not this path); UI as above. Smoke and `test-world all` in both reasoners: see the end of this entry.
`npm run test:smoke` exit 0 (82 tests, 18.8 s). `test-world all`: matrix 80 failing rows, ops 79 (the landing: 80 and 79; the same rows). Invariants green: undo per request (undo-redo 100 percent), live-state, network (smoke has no network attempt).

## 2026-11-14 LAZY-LOAD-3: the reading model on demand, one fetch of the shared modules (proved at the server), bundled-geo with the geo world (reviewer 12:25 items 1-3)
**1. The reading model and onnxruntime.** The first message does not need them: with `waitForModel: false` the rules answer until the model is ready (operational set: 95.4 % right with the rules alone, 98.6 % with dispatcher and normalizer, so the model is wanted for garbled sentences, not for the first greeting). Before: the model (65 MB) and then the wasm (14.5 MB) started on an idle CPU right after the first paint, in every start. Now `startModels()` in `docs/webchat/app.mjs` starts them (once) when (1) a reply is not read cleanly (no `supported` status, or an unparsed segment), (2) after `MODEL_IDLE_MS` = 30 s, (3) the helper-model switch is turned on, (4) Settings > Models "Load now" (as before); the step "Reading model" reads "loads when a message needs it" meanwhile. Helper-model semantics unchanged (off = rules only, on = used once loaded). Spec 06 updated.
**2. Fetched twice.** Measured at the server (not by summing CDP targets): on a first visit with no service worker (`?psys2nosw=1`, GitHub-Pages-like headers) `sopworld.mjs` and `en.facts.generated.mjs` reach the server once each; the page's avatar imports them after the engine worker's request filled the HTTP cache, and with the service worker they come from its cache. The "twice" is the page, worker and service-worker targets each reporting one request. The page does need both (the avatar's motion planner and `facelogic` read them), so no code change; the new scenario `first` counts each URL once on a first visit and fails if that changes.
**3. bundled-geo.mjs.** `open-words.mjs` no longer imports it; `worlds/geo.map/hooks.mjs` calls `provideBundledGeo(BUNDLED_GEO)` when the world's ops load (the only world with a `catalog=k.geo` lexicon), so the map's offline places work as before once the world is loaded (a reading that names a place loads the world through the word index or the second reading). `tests/open-words.test.mjs` pass; `tests/geo-places.test.mjs` "nothing is loaded before the host settles the needs" fails with and without this change (checked by reverting it): not caused here.
**Probe (Chrome, local server, 40 s at 1 MB/s cold and warm; 25 s unthrottled "reviewer-like", no catalog route).** Before (HEAD 75c07a96): unthrottled 25 s: 190 requests, 88.1 MB at the server (68 MB model, 14.8 MB wasm); throttled 40 s: 5.1 MB, the model 29 of 65 MB when the probe ended, the popup busy the whole time. After: unthrottled 25 s: 180 requests, 4.6 MB (no model, no wasm); throttled cold and warm 40 s: 4.6-4.8 MB (the idle trigger starts the model at about 36 s), ready at 5.5 s, `bundled-geo.mjs` not requested. The boot test `cold` (13/13), `lazy`, `warm` and the new `first` (7/7) pass; the cold test allows the `talk` bundle (the warm-up reads "hello" after the input is enabled; it was already fetched at boot before this change, which made the old check fail).

- **Table (71 failing rows):** the ORIGINAL sentence reads right in 44 (wording gap, knowledge exists), fails in 27 (knowledge gap: animal sound 13/13, other single 13/25, story question 1/10). MiniLM first-accepted proposal: 14 right (19.7%, any of 5: 17), 10 accepted but read as another meaning, 11 accepted not read, 28 all rejected by the checker, 8 no proposal. - **Findings:** (1) at most 62% of the gap is wording, at least 38% knowledge; a proposer with a raw encoder gets a third of the wording part. (2) The checker rejected a proposal the rules read right in 13 rows (currency word, number word counted as changed value) and cannot see a name swap (the vocabulary knows ana / mia / tom): a first run without the names guard "rescued" several story rows by an answer that did not depend on the name. (3) 10 accepted proposals change the meaning (notation letters are not bound as values: "G's major scale" read as "D major scale"). (4) Raw MiniLM is not better than TF-IDF at rank 1. ## 2026-11-15 FIRST-TURN: "put on a hat" as the first message ended as a runaway (ledger row "first-turn runaway")
- **Cause (evidence).** Reproduced in headless Chrome on the real page (real catalog, phone viewport, fresh session): 8.0 s, "Stopped a runaway computation in stage knowledge" (live shows `end`: the final guard check is where an exhausted deadline is noticed). `reply.perf` of the working run: `knowledge` 4.7 s of 4.7 s total; the request log shows 81 `k.faces` shards plus 14 `k.words` shards requested one after another (about 120 ms apart): `facts.wires` awaited each shard in a loop, and the preload of the typed needs of the avatar world (`preloadThings` -> `knowledge.load` -> `faces()`) runs inside the turn clock. Not a spin: compute of the turn was ~40 ms. Later turns find the faces cached.
- **Fix (general).** (1) `guard.untimed(work)` (src/formalizer/guard.mjs): a load waits outside the turn limit (deadline moved by the wait, cap 30 s, listener for the host). Used for the typed-needs preload (`knowledge-lookup.mjs`) and the vocabulary load at the start of `send` (`dialog/index.mjs`). (2) The engine worker forwards it as `turn-wait`; the page watchdog (`app.mjs`) pauses on `turn-wait` and `world-load` and resumes with the rest of the limit; page deadline, backstop and client timer get the cap on top. (3) `facts.wires` fetches the shards of one read together. The "network never changes a reading" invariant is untouched (same reads, same order of processing; the 6 s catalog bound `within` is unchanged), the turn guard still ends real runaways at the limit.
- **Checks.** `tests/first-turn-load-wait.test.mjs` (3 tests; 2 fail without the fix); `scripts/test-webchat-first-turn.mjs` (Chrome, delayed fixture catalog: answered, no runaway notice, shards requested together; the last check fails without the fix). Chrome repro after the fix: first turn 5.0 s on this box with the real catalog, answered "I already have a bow hat.", no notice. Not done: warm the needs of a world in idle time after it loads (would make the first turn near-instant).
- **Finished (second worker after a rate-limit stop).** Webchat rebuilt; `tests/first-turn-load-wait.test.mjs` + `tests/turn-guard.test.mjs` 12/12; `scripts/test-webchat-first-turn.mjs` (Chrome, phone, 4x throttle, 2.5 s per catalog request) all pass: first turn answered in 6.4 s ("I already have a bow hat."), no runaway notice, 38 face shards requested within 347 ms; `npm run test:smoke` 88/88, exit 0. Pre-existing on HEAD, unrelated: 4 failures in draw-from-facts / knowledge-lookup (catalog k.objects out of date, composite ops, built-in kinds as facts, catalog-hit refusal).

## 2026-11-15 FOREIGN READINGS + RETIRED ROWS (spec 16 section 14; reviewer 23:50 items "measurement integrity" and "new owner export")
Runtime, general mechanisms only (`src/dialog/foreign-reading.mjs`, after `reviewSegments`, before execution; `PSYS2_FOREIGN=off` for A/B):
1. **Full reading.** A world other than the open tab's (with a tab of its own, not ambient, not named in the message) acts only on a full reading: no spelling correction, no voice rewrite, no ignored word, no gerund / dropped subject reframed as a command (`seg.reframed`, set where `readingVariants` reframes), no best effort, no word left by the STRICT typed reading (`unreadStrict`: section 13 with `rest` typed too), no empty slot value, not a fragment. Otherwise the clause is unparsed (`seg.foreign`) and takes the honest path (the tab world's `outOfScope`, else "I did not understand").
2. **Mood.** `lang.mood.statement` (new phrase group in lang.common: i have, i like, i am, my name is ...; wishes are not in it) + `ctx.lang.statement`: a request reading of a first-person statement is refused in every world (navigation too), unless the pattern's own frame reads the speaker (`readsSpeaker`: inline literal or the world's own macro starting with "i": "I have to tidy my room" stays a to-do, "I am lost" stays help); verbless list pieces go with it; reply "That sounds like something about you. I cannot keep facts about you here." (Romanian reply added, informal singular).
3. **Fragment.** One letter / only articles is never a slot value of another tab's world.
Measurement: result files carry `build` + `tree` (`scripts/lib/measure-build.mjs`, hash of src, worlds, knowledge, judge, set); `real-set.mjs record` and `learning-curve.mjs --record` refuse a stale result (`--allow-stale`); `tests/real-result-fresh.test.mjs` fails when a committed default result is older than its tree (NOTE: every change to src/worlds/knowledge now needs `node scripts/real-set.mjs run --reasoner matrix` and `--reasoner ops`, about 1 min each, before `npm test` passes). The 72 judged rows that need a removed world are RETIRED (kept, `retired`, old check in `check_pre_cut`, new check = clean refusal: unchanged + `world_not` the surviving tab worlds), out of the headline, reported on their own line (`report`, `record`, learning curve). r0641 "draw a house" of the profile dialogue stays in scope (its expectation is art.draw only), so 72 not 73. The runner shows removed tabs as Talk and reads tabWorld before the turn. The 25 owner-log checks that only forbid a reply get `world_not` (tab worlds other than the check's and the tab's). `visibleState` ignores empty lazy world states (`plan.seating` / `plan.timeline` appearing as `{}` on any turn: the owner export's finding 4, left to the other agent). ## 2026-11-15 P2b: shipped-mode "too complex" on real draw turns (LEARNED-MEM-INDEX)
Cause: in the shipped mode (encoder formalizer, catalog pinned) 39 real turns ran out of the step budget, all at site `learned.mem` (r0080-r0132 of owner-log b, r0301, r0358-r0371, r0632; r0633 then failed in a cascade). `withLearned` (src/knowledge/learned.mjs, the catalog overlay of spec 23) scanned the WHOLE session memory on every catalog lookup (`memWires`), and a turn makes about 2 000 lookups (`session.things` sync peeks every object of the picture through `aspectsOf` / `lend`, again for every candidate reading, translation candidate and encoder pass). The memory grows with the picture, so the ticks grew with lookups x wires: quadratic in the session length. The rules diagnostic never showed it (no catalog overlay load at that scale).
Evidence (scratchpad p2b/probe.mjs, a draw session with the test catalog): learned.mem per turn 4.6 k at 14 wires, 60 k at 50, 209 k at 86, 249 k at 102 wires (total turn ticks 262 k); after the fix 442 / 1.5 k / 3.0 k / 3.1 k (total 16 k). Failing stack: `memWires <- forWord <- o.peek <- lend (session.things/ops.mjs) <- aspectsOf`.
Fix (general, no limit raised): the overlay reads the memory through an index (records by name) built once per contents of the memory. `WireStore.memo(key, build)` (src/interpreter/memory.mjs) keeps derived data until the next `add` (retractions and replacements are adds) and shares it with dry-run clones (wires are immutable). Build ticks `learned.mem` per wire, a lookup per candidate word; returned records are copies. Spec 06 "Compute budgets" bullet LEARNED-MEM-INDEX. Regression test tests/learned-mem-budget.test.mjs with injected budgets (fails on the old code: 2 521 ticks against a 60-per-wire budget; the starved site still ends the turn as too complex with the picture restored).
Numbers (real set, shipped mode, matrix, seed 20261115, catalog ab3b2ab): before 123/181 right (partly 12, wrong 46), retired 65/72, 39 too-complex turns; after 131/181 (partly 12, wrong 38), retired 65/72, 0 too-complex. 44 rows changed outcome, none got worse in verdict (8 wrong -> right incl. r0092, r0098, r0113, r0115, r0122, r0125, r0632, r0633; the open owner rows now execute -> `changed`, to be looked at by hand; r0358/r0360/r0361 now other_world instead of not_understood). ms p50 122 -> 135 (turns that bailed now do their work), max 2 740 -> 2 337. Result file training/results/real-2026-11-15-matrix-p2after.json (the headline file is P1's). test-world all 58 raw / 40 first (= baseline). Smoke: pass after the webchat rebuild (only the freshness check failed before it).

## 2026-11-15 SCAN-PROFILE / OVERLAY-MEMO / LEGEND-MEMO / SPELL-MEMO: the other per-lookup scans (reviewer 02:05 item 2)
- **Profile (new).** `reply.perf.ticks = { total, sites }`; the real-set runner passes a budget per turn and records `pos` + `tk { total, sites }` per row (12 busiest kept) and a top-level per-site profile over all sites (`scripts/lib/tick-profile.mjs`: sum, share, p50, max, mean early (pos < 10) / late (pos >= 20), growth = late/early, slope per position). `node scripts/real-set.mjs sites [<result>]` prints top by total and by growth. `diff` ignores `tk`.
- **How each site was confirmed.** Growth in the real set is confounded (late turns are 67 % Romanian vs 18 % early), so each suspect was checked by a replay: the same probe messages at 0/13/25/37/49/61 objects in one growing draw session (snapshot, send with a budget, restore; scratchpad scan/probe.mjs), and late real turns replayed in their session vs in a fresh session (scan/fresh.mjs), with stack sampling of the site (scan/session.mjs).
- **Sites fixed (each indexed / memoised: built once, invalidated on change, copies handed out, a hit = 1 tick; no limit raised; turn guard and invariants kept):**
  1. `learned.mem` + `things.aspects` + `commonsense.habitat` (OVERLAY-MEMO, c6307ba3). After LEARNED-MEM-INDEX a lookup was cheap but there were still thousands per turn: `session.things` `sync` runs on every operation call and recomputed every object's aspects (peek of the kind, `ancestors` = a walk of up to 6 is-a levels, a peek of each ancestor through `lend`), and art.draw's `sameLayer` asked `habitat` for every object near every spot tried. Probe "make the tree bigger": learned.mem 4 426 ticks at 13 objects -> 22 090 at 61 (old) vs 3 298 -> 3 586 (new). Fix: `withLearned` keeps `peek` / `ancestors` / `memo(name, key, build)` answers under the key (catalog `generation()` — a GenMap in facts.mjs that moves with every settled lookup or reset — | lessons key) inside the memory store's `memo` (dropped on add, shared with dry-run clones). session.things memoises a thing's aspects by (kind, name, attribute names, has parts, declared, attrTypes) and the aspects an ancestor lends; `habitat` per word. Test tests/overlay-memo-budget.test.mjs (fails on the old code: learned.mem 1 518 against the 12-object ticks + 20/object).
  2. `index.chain` (LEGEND-MEMO, da1f83d8): `Legends.chain` / `tryResolveKey` walked the type chain on every `ctx.val`; art.draw `ensure` -> `loadUsualPlaces` re-reads the common.sense facts on every referents call (each candidate reading). Memo per type / (type, key) until `_ensure` rebuilds (key memo bounded 50 k).
  3. `spell.edit` (SPELL-MEMO, 59155098): spellCorrect / spellCandidates / spellAlternates rebuilt the candidate list and the known set (O(vocab), unticked) and scanned the vocabulary for the same unknown word in every world at every stage (lenient, dispatcher validator, capability read, suspect check, candidates). WeakMap per vocabulary object (rebuilt on a size change, 20 k words bounded) of candidates, known set and neighbours `[{w, d}]`; ranking unchanged. Test tests/scan-memo-budget.test.mjs covers 2 and 3 (both fail on the old code).

## 2026-11-15 Pin follow-ups: one diagram per request (timelines), `user_facing` filter, outline nodes that fit (coordinator; reviewer 04:50)
- **Timelines, matrix vs ops (dg30/dg31/dg51).** Not a reasoner difference: `composedDiagram` seeds each request with `Math.random`, and `composeForRequest` tried six seeds from it, so the library's seeded fill order chose between the two timeline fills of the planets (`k.space.body order` by=distance, `size_rank` by=size) differently from run to run, on either reasoner (reproduced: ops drew Jupiter-first on one run, matrix on the next). The "labels off one axis" failure was the size order (Jupiter...Mercury), not a placement fault. Random rows with 0 arrows were timelines, whose kind says `edges=none`. Fix (shared path, `src/knowledge/diagram-world.mjs`): every fill of the kind is tried through a view of the World that holds only that fill; the pick is the fill whose type, key or `by=` names a request word, then the knowledge's order; the seed now only places a free layout. A kind with `edges=none` and `structure=sequence` (timeline: "events in order along a line", each "a dot on the line") carries `line`, and `engineNodes` joins its nodes in order with plain segments.
- **`user_facing=false` (Q17 (3)).** `offered(world, fill, topic)`: a fact with `user_facing=false`, or a topic that names one through the fill's topic key (slot `type=k.procedures.method by=name`), is never drawn for a named topic, sampled, or offered by the dice. The bundle (`scripts/build-bundled-diagrams.mjs`) now carries the referenced facts plus both type schemas, whole, only where the facts carry the key (k.procedures: +46 lines). Lesson: a partial schema (only the identity slot `method id=true`) made all steps of one method one fact, and the whole world was refused.

## 2026-11-15 slice 1: the door owns the timeline (reviewer 19:05, 19:40; acts worker)
The 22 smoke tests the door had put on the legacy list are real breaks; they are off the list and pass, generically, at the one place plans run (no per-world code in the door):
- **One plan = one undo step**: `_doorBegin` takes every world's state and the library's mark of the turn before a plan or a declared operation runs; `_sendCore` takes them (`override.before`) and records the request as a frame (`Discourse.recordDoorFrame`, the same frame a reader's request leaves). A **revision replaces** the step of the result it revises. A **question** is no step (unchanged: no frame).
- **Undo / redo are acts of the timeline** (k.actions undo / redo, read by readRequest): inside the turn (`override.run`), the timeline answers first (`Discourse.undoRedo`: redo of a timeline step, "undo the whole message", "undo the house" with its yes / no question, answered by the dialogue before any reading), else the world's own undo / redo bound in request.sop (`psys2.op world= act=undo op=undo|diagramUndo|docUndo`). An undo naming something no step did, or with unread words, takes nothing back.
- **Tool binding as data**: `psys2.op world= act= [of=] op=` (Drawing: `act=make of=page op=newDrawing` for "start a new page"; k.actions "start" / "begin" = make as local rows, Q43 [KNOW]). Drawing declares `sky` (drawn by the board's own background operation) and `on=attribute` for make (a colour said is drawn: "draw a red house"; "make the sky red" colours the band).
- **Things said together** ("draw a sky and a sun"): stand-in `coordinated()` plans each wanted kind as its own request (library drops all but the first, Q42 (4) [LIB]); the Drawing's executor draws each kind as one step of its history, so "undo" takes the last one back.
- **A partly read turn never acts**, and the reply names the clauses ("I understood "clear everything", but not "zork the plimp", so I did nothing."), cut at the language world's joiners (`clausesOf`).
- An executor's `cannot` is now said even when the act's reply is plain (P8).
- tests/model-timeouts: r2 goes back to Talk (the first message opens the declared Drawing tab, where the door runs no model) — the test's purpose (timeouts counted per session) is unchanged.
- [LIB] asks: questions.md Q42 (runPlan owns the timeline; undo / redo / named steps as a w.dialogue mechanism; tool binding with preconditions and effects; coordinated kinds; the door's reply strings as reply facts). Patch smells still in the door: reply literals (Q42 (5)).

## 2026-11-15 slice 2: the open state as facts, acts on things (move / change / remove), RP5b/RP5c off the legacy list (acts worker)
**Generic pieces (one path in the door, `_doorThings` in src/dialog/index.mjs; request.mjs stand-ins, each a Q42 [LIB] ask):**
- **The open state as facts** (`stateWorld`): the things a world shows through its `referents` operation (which every schema world has: id, kind, name, attributes) are told into a fork of its live request World as instances of its declared kinds (attributes under their slots; a word for a slot by core.word). The fork is the spell repair's other world (names of things are candidates) and the planner's world for a new request (places and referents). factsOf reads it.
- **References** (`referTo`): a run of unread words that is a thing's name ("work done", "results"), a kind said (plural: all; one there: it; several: the salient ones, else **asked**: "Which circle do you mean: ...?"), the world's own whole ("the drawing", "the diagram": the kind its std.schema.world name means), "everything" (a pronoun of the language world with refers=all), "it"/"them" (the last act's things, else what the last result made, else the salient ones). Definiteness from w.lang.en.det definite=yes (`definiteKind`), which also replaced the two English regexes of the door ("the tree" names a thing of the open world).
- **Acts on things**: place / change / remove read from k.actions; "make X red" is the change sense of the verb (k.actions lists make under change) when X is there and named definitely or by "it"; a turn of only roles after an act on things continues it ("higher", "and smaller"); an act with no object takes the last act's things. Honours per act and kind lineage (request.sop `std.schema.honours act=place|change|remove`), roles: place (a region value, a direction, a thing of the state), attribute + value, size (a value or a relative step). **Tool binding** `psys2.op act=place|change|remove op=requestAct` — the one executor path; the world's `requestAct` is its adapter from the generic roles to its own primitives (see below).
- **Language data stand-ins** (src/lang/en.request.local.mjs, Q43 [KNOW]): direction cues up/down/higher/lower/left/right, "to the middle", "to <value>", "the colour/size of <thing>", "into <thing>", pronouns refers=all ("everything") and refers=any ("something", "whatever you want"), verbs start/begin = make.
- **Make**: "draw something random / whatever you want" is the world's own whole; a general whole ("a random picture") is sampled among the wholes the world plans, its own before the catalog's (`psys2.door`); a place said by a kind the world makes but that is not there ("3 fish in water") is made by the world; a place and an extent read from the same words ("in the corner") is honoured by the place; "in the diagram" on the Diagram is the world itself (`withoutSelfPlace`); things of kinds on the Diagram are plain shapes ("draw three circles" -> "I drew 3 circles."), a diagram of the knowledge is asked for as a diagram; an arrangement (a named layout with only its regions and a count of its parts) comes before a revision; the reader's repaired words name the regions; a new thing does not take the dialogue values of the last one (its colour).
- **Replies**: a diagram's topic (a label of the knowledge) is a name in the reply, never translated word by word (`namedParts`); the names of things in an act's reply likewise. The Romanian replies of RP5c / RP5b are composed again.
- **World adapters (answer to the coordinator's check):** `worlds/diagram.sketch/engine.mjs requestAct` (+~45 lines) and `worlds/art.draw/engine.mjs requestAct` / `skyColour` (+~90) take ids already resolved and roles already read; they decide nothing about references, kinds or plans. They exist because the worlds' existing operations take a text phrase and re-read it with their own NP reader (diagram engine `move`/`set`/`delete` read `r.text`; the board's `move`/`recolor`/`remove` read `args.phrase`): the adapters call the primitives under them (engine commands `move/set/delete` with targets; the board's `placeRegion`, `placeRelative`, colour, size, the ground band). They map role values to the world's own vocabulary (place value -> engine region name, size step -> engine size) — that mapping is a declaration that belongs in request.sop once the library has typed tool binding with preconditions and effects (Q42 (3)); the avatar would then only declare. The executor parts of planRequest added for this slice (sky/ground drawn by the board's background operation, plain shapes on the Diagram, the place in the user's words before the plan's) are the worlds' own primitives, bound as they were.
- **Fixture** (scripts/owner-session.mjs): the owner's state of the `setup` line is built by the readers (`request: false`): it is the fixture, not a measured turn. Without it the door's turns of the owner session named things that did not exist (shapes[name=results] undefined), so the door-merge numbers RO 7/43 under-measured the move turns; the turns won below are attributed with that in mind (each move turn needs both the fixture's names and the move act).
- Test change: none besides the model-timeouts one of slice 1. Legacy list 205 -> 187 (removed when they pass: RP5b x3, RP5c x2, astra-session x2, clauses-in-sequence undo, discourse-memory JSON, draw undo, open-tab-prior "something random", scene-referents whole path, talk-transfers, turn-scope, world-aware choose, and more).

- **Tools (JS, no words, no request reading)**: Drawing `removeThings`, `moveThings`, `setThings`; Diagram `removeShapes`, `moveShapes`, `setShapes` (the engine's commands). The request is read with the mirrored view as `ctx.state` (readTurn `state`, as toolSession does), so names of things are references. A verbless fragment (`reaction: 'continue'`, "a sun" after "draw a fish") is a new request with the dialogue's act; a revision replaces the last result only when `rev.replace` says so. - **Scenes on the binding** (worlds/art.draw/request.sop): `startScene(kind, place)` bound `act=make of=pond of=forest of=garden`; `addThings` takes `whole<-step.in` (the things of a scene stand together: next to its first thing, else in its region); `remove` / `place` / `change` of=picture act on the scene's things. The library plans the scene as a whole with its parts from the catalog's `k.expect.make` / `k.expect.part` (by join), "less trees" goes through its count revision. The view lists a scene after its things (`{ id, kind }`; things carry `in`), so the inverse of a plan (a revision, a rollback) takes the things back first; a scene left without things is gone (kept as gone, so taking it back again is no refusal). Catalog things the board draws (butterfly) are a `composite:` kind inside the primitive; the view says kinds by name.
